title: Attainability under coordinate polarization
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f\colon\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $b\in\{−1,1\}$, and choose $i\in J$ and $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$. Define the coordinate-polarized function $f_i^{\mathrm{pol}}$ by taking, at an input $z$, the maximum of $f$ at the two inputs obtained by setting coordinate $i$ to $1$ and $-1$ if $z_i=1$, and their minimum if $z_i=-1$. If one can obtain output $b$ from $f_i^{\mathrm{pol}}$ at some input agreeing with $x$ outside $J$, then one can obtain output $b$ from $f$ at some input agreeing with $x$ outside $J$.
hypotheses_covered: The polarized function can attain $b$ while agreeing with $x$ outside $J$
